translations.t0002: The garage log contains no exit entry for SG 482 117 on 10 October in the provided extract; the exact exit time of Vogel's vehicle is not supported by a garage log entry.
translations.t0003: How did Vogel acquire the technical knowledge (decompression behaviour of K3, snapshot deletion procedure) required to carry out the act? Ticket JI-SEC-486 was reported by her, which suggests some familiarity with the phenomenon but does not prove it.
translations.t0004: The exfiltration device (USB identifier per Forensics Annex B) was not cross-referenced against known devices belonging to persons within the investigation circle; the recipient of the data (Kestrel contact person) has not been identified.

translations.t0006: Lukas Hofer and Andrin Caduff remain open as alternative perpetrator hypotheses with complete perpetrator knowledge and unsubstantiated alibis for the night of the offence; a conclusive exculpation is not available for either of these two individuals.

translations.t0011: Slides containing path mappings or enumerations of sensitive artefacts must never be embedded in distributed presentations. Board decks with a classification of ≥ CONFIDENTIAL undergo a four-eyes security sign-off before distribution.
translations.t0012: Prevents the complete Real/Decoy mapping from entering circulating documents at all — and thereby prevents one of the earliest information leaks.
translations.t0013: Does not protect against verbal disclosure in the board meeting itself; board members who have already received the slide retain the information.
translations.t0014: First and most far-reaching information leak: without Slide 11, the mapping is considerably harder for outsiders to reconstruct.
translations.t0015: Restrict internal documentation of sensitive mappings to need-to-know.
translations.t0016: The Real/Decoy mapping was published on Confluence with eng-all permissions, making it accessible to 9 accounts.
translations.t0017: Favre publishes the Storage-Integrity-Controls page on Confluence (sequence index 2).
translations.t0018: Pages containing production paths, checkpoint structures, or decoy mappings automatically receive restricted visibility (Security team only) upon creation. Confluence space defaults for #eng must not grant read permissions to eng-all when the content is classified as sensitive.
translations.t0019: Limits the circle of people who know the mapping to those with an explicit need-to-know.
translations.t0020: Permission errors through manual override remain possible; persons within the approved circle can pass on the information.
translations.t0021: Second major expansion of the knowledge circle — and documented in the system, therefore automatically discoverable.
translations.t0022: Prohibit audit log interruptions without redundant backup.
translations.t0023: The audit collector and the SIEM cold tier were deactivated simultaneously, resulting in no audit trail for nine hours — precisely the window in which the copying took place.
translations.t0024: INFRA-2291 provides for the collector and SIEM cold tier to be shut down simultaneously (sequence index 3).
translations.t0025: Before any planned collector shutdown, at least one independent logging sink (e.g. syslog forwarding to a separate tier) must remain active. Changes to logging infrastructure that result in a complete audit gap are not permitted without board-level approval.
translations.t0026: Substantially reduces the blind window for attackers; a parallel log captures at least device events and network activity.
translations.t0027: A determined insider with admin rights can disable secondary sinks as well; 100% coverage without hardware-based logging is not achievable.
translations.t0028: The complete audit gap is the central enabling condition: without logs, the identity of the operator cannot be determined to this day (README-L27).
translations.t0029: Technically block USB mass storage on workstations.
translations.t0030: A portable block device was connected directly to a workstation on the engineering floor and a bulk copy job was started locally — without any control triggering.
translations.t0031: Bulk copy job starts on scratch-02; the target device is an externally connected portable block device (sequence index 9).
translations.t0032: Block USB mass-storage device classes on workstations on the engineering floor via MDM/endpoint policy, or restrict them to explicitly registered devices with an approval workflow. Connection of an unregistered block device triggers an immediate alert.
translations.t0033: Prevents or delays the connection of unregistered devices; in the alerting scenario an early detection point is created.
translations.t0034: Users with physical access and administrative rights can circumvent policies; BYOD devices in the colo (HD-3999) are subject to different controls.
translations.t0035: Without this control, any person with physical access to the engineering floor can exfiltrate data in the terabyte range without passing any network control.
translations.t0036: Control and log physical access to the engineering floor.
translations.t0037: No camera system on the engineering floor, side entrance permanently open, badge system unreliable — the identity of the operator cannot be determined.
translations.t0038: Job started from workstation console on the engineering floor, no identification possible (sequence index 9); alley door reportedly always wedged open according to interview (IV03-L37).
translations.t0039: Install camera surveillance at the entrance to the engineering floor and at the alley door. Equip the side entrance with an automatic closing mechanism that triggers an alert if it remains open for more than 30 seconds. Regularly test badge readers for functionality.
translations.t0040: Creates an identification point even when digital logs are absent; deterrent effect for insiders.
translations.t0041: Cameras can be covered or bypassed; identification requires that the recordings are secured and have not been tampered with.
translations.t0042: Direct cause of the failure to identify the perpetrator; but a downstream control — prevention through earlier measures (USB block, logging) is more effective.
translations.t0043: Do not announce maintenance windows with audit gaps to a broad audience.
translations.t0044: The migration window and the associated nine-hour audit gap were communicated in Jira, Slack #eng-infra, and at standup — approximately 40 people became aware of it.
translations.t0045: Ticket INFRA-2291 and related announcements inform ~40 people about the window (sequence index 3).
translations.t0046: Time windows during which logging infrastructure is shut down are communicated only to directly involved persons (assignee, security sign-off, on-call). No announcement in general channels or standups.
translations.t0047: Reduces the circle of people who know a blind-window date and can deliberately exploit it for an exfiltration.
translations.t0048: Internal communications cannot be fully sealed; persons with system access can also derive windows from logs.
translations.t0049: Reduces attack opportunity through information minimisation, but prevents only opportunistic exploitation, not a planned insider attack.
translations.t0050: Log scratch volumes with session and user context.
translations.t0051: Scratch volumes are not connected to the audit pipeline; no user session context is recorded — forensic identification of the perpetrator is impossible.
translations.t0052: No user session record present on scratch-02; forensics cannot identify the operator (sequence indices 9 and 13).
translations.t0053: Integrate scratch volumes and associated workstation consoles into a separate, write-protected audit log that records session start, logged-in user, connected devices (USB IDs), and launched processes. This log is mirrored to a system isolated from the engineering network.
translations.t0054: Enables post-hoc identification of the operator and substantially reduces investigation time.
translations.t0055: Effective only for future incidents; the existing evidentiary gap in this case remains. An insider with root privileges can manipulate local logs before mirroring if the isolation is incomplete.

translations.t0074: Caduff's own assessment that stealing the weights would be unnecessary for him is an assertion, but plausible given his seniority.
translations.t0075: The replan email documents that the closure of the research line was a board decision and was not framed as a personal attack.
translations.t0076: The investigator noted the motive as grounds for suspicion; Caduff's internal state ultimately remains unverifiable.
translations.t0077: No independent document confirms Caduff's presence in St. Gallen during the offence window (23:10–05:58 CEST). There is no card payment, no garage log (no car), and no witness. The visit to the climbing gym on Saturday is likewise unsubstantiated. However, all contrary evidence is also absent: no card payment, no garage log entry, and no witness places him in Zurich or at the scene.
translations.t0078: No independent source confirms his presence in St. Gallen on Friday evening/Saturday night; the climbing gym visit and Sunday dinner are likewise unsubstantiated.
translations.t0079: Caduff's knowledge of the staging path is legitimate as an insider since before 2023. His knowledge of the Decoy/Real mapping is less clear: he claims to have known only that decoys exist, not which ones. He explicitly onboarded himself on the known paths. He says he did not read the Confluence page, which is neither confirmed nor refuted. He claims not to have seen the board deck, which is plausible (he is not a board member and not in the distribution list). His comment in JI-DATA-1930 ('Improve error message on decompress-on-write overflow') documents that he was familiar with the decompression problem.
translations.t0080: Caduff claims not to have known the specific Real/Decoy mapping — only the existence of decoys was known to him.
translations.t0081: Caduff denies having accessed the board deck; the distribution list (board, CEO, presenting executive, deck assembler) does not include him.
translations.t0082: The board deck distribution list excludes Caduff.
translations.t0083: Caduff commented on a ticket concerning the decompression overflow — documenting his knowledge of this technical detail.
translations.t0084: Yannick confirms that he published the mapping on Confluence in March with eng-all permissions.
translations.t0085: The Real/Decoy mapping was potentially accessible to Caduff via the Confluence page (eng-all, 9 accounts, 16 views), even though he denies having read it.
translations.t0086: The nine accounts are not identified; Caduff's account could be among them but this has not been established.
translations.t0087: Caduff has no registered vehicle in the garage log; all card transactions attributable to him show SBB and local St. Gallen payments, supporting the claim of 'no car'. The absence of a vehicle does not, however, rule out physical presence: the alley door is unsecured and Caduff himself demonstrates knowledge of this through multiple helpdesk tickets and Slack posts.
translations.t0088: Card transaction SBB St. Gallen documents use of rail as a means of transport.
translations.t0089: Caduff filed multiple helpdesk tickets about the alley door — he is very familiar with how it works.
translations.t0090: Caduff publicly warned about the open door — this is more consistent with the behaviour of a security-conscious person than with someone who intended to use the door for the offence.
translations.t0091: The repeated tickets could alternatively be interpreted as gathering information about the access point, even though the more obvious explanation is frustration about a security problem.
translations.t0092: Caduff claims to have been in his apartment in St. Gallen during the night of the offence (Friday 10.10. evening to Saturday 11.10. early morning).
translations.t0093: No card payment, no garage log (no car), no witness, and no digital trace places Caduff in St. Gallen or at the scene during the night of the offence. The absence of evidence is neither incriminating nor exculpatory.
translations.t0094: Caduff claims to have started a read-only eval sweep via VPN at approximately 22:00 CEST.
translations.t0095: The sweep is entered in the calendar and publicly announced in Slack. Both are consistent with the claim and document the intention, but not the actual execution from home. VPN logs do not exist for the relevant time window according to the forensic report (audit logging disabled). A calendar entry documents a booking, not a presence.
translations.t0096: Caduff claims to have visited a climbing gym on Saturday 11.10.
translations.t0097: No card payment for a climbing gym on 11.10.2025 found in the card feed. The visit is therefore neither confirmed nor refuted.
translations.t0098: Caduff claims to own no car and not to drive.
translations.t0099: The garage log contains no entry with a licence plate registered to Caduff. His card feed consistently shows SBB and local purchases in St. Gallen, with no fuel or car park payments outside St. Gallen in the relevant period. The garage helpdesk entry ('keep trying to sell me a space') corroborates the claim.
translations.t0100: Caduff claims not to have known the Real/Decoy mapping and not to have read the Confluence page.
translations.t0101: The nine accounts that read the Confluence page are not listed by name. Caduff's account may or may not be among them. The claim is neither confirmed nor refuted.
translations.t0102: Caduff has legitimate insider access to the undocumented staging path (since before 2023, confirmed by his own statement and by Hofer). He knows the decompression behaviour of the pipeline (documented by his comment on JI-SEC-486). Regarding the Real/Decoy mapping: he denies knowledge of the specific mapping; the board deck distribution list excludes him; the Confluence page was technically accessible to him (eng-all), but his read access has not been established. The statement 'Iris told everyone in research not to open anything that looked unusual' explains why he avoided the decoys — without knowing the exact list.
translations.t0103: Caduff had technical read access to the real checkpoints (authorised by Hofer). Physical access to the engineering floor is possible without a car (alley door unsecured, reachable by bicycle or public transport). No garage log entry constrains him. The exfiltration was carried out from a local console — physical presence would have been required.
translations.t0104: The offence window (23:10–05:58 CEST) falls entirely at night. Caduff claims to have been at home in St. Gallen. This is neither confirmed nor refuted. His eval sweep start (22:05 CEST per Slack) falls shortly before the copying began (23:10 CEST), which would theoretically be temporally compatible with physical presence at the scene from approximately 23:10 — but equally consistent with legitimate remote work from home.
translations.t0105: The alibi for the night of the offence remains entirely unsubstantiated: no card payment, no witness, and no digital trace places Caduff in St. Gallen between 23:10 and 05:58 CEST.
translations.t0106: Caduff theoretically had access to the Real/Decoy mapping via the Confluence page (eng-all, 9 accounts), even though his read access has not been established.
translations.t0107: The temporal coincidence between the publicly announced eval sweep (22:05 CEST) and the start of the copying operation (23:10 CEST) cannot be resolved through independent logs.
translations.t0108: The known points of suspicion (high access rate, motive, no alibi) are partially explicable as harmless (authorised paper sweep, board decision without personal grievance, no car). However, positive exculpatory evidence for the night of the offence is entirely absent. There is no independent evidence placing Caduff at another location throughout the entire offence window. The alibi is not refuted, but it is also not confirmed. At the same time there is no positive evidence against him: no garage log, no card payment, no forensic fingerprint placing him at the console. The case remains open.
translations.t0109: Caduff's conspicuous checkpoint accesses are plausibly explicable by a legitimately approved research project, and his behaviour (public announcement of the sweep, repeated complaints about the open door) is more consistent with innocence than with criminal planning. However, his alibi for the night of the offence is entirely unsubstantiated, and the combination of insider knowledge, absent alibi, and temporal coincidence is insufficient for either exculpation or incrimination — the case remains open.
translations.t0110: The nine accounts that read the Confluence page are not known by name; Caduff's knowledge of the Real/Decoy mapping through this channel cannot be ruled out.
translations.t0111: VPN logs and audit logs for the night of the offence do not exist (INFRA-2291); whether the eval sweep was actually running from home cannot be verified.
translations.t0112: The climbing gym visit on Saturday 11.10. is not supported by a card payment; it remains unclear where Caduff actually was after the end of the offence window (05:58 CEST).
translations.t0113: The exfiltration required physical presence on the engineering floor; without a car, Caduff would have been reliant on a bicycle or public transport — both theoretically possible at night, but not documented.
translations.t0114: The unknown vehicle in the garage log of 11.10. (GAR-L3017, licence plate partially illegible 'SG 482 1?7', exit at 05:09 facility time = 06:09 CEST corrected) cannot be attributed to any person and could — without any positive evidence — be relevant.
translations.t0115: Bernasconi claims to have driven from Winterthur to Flims early on Saturday morning (~06:00). Are there fuel receipts, card payments, or garage log entries confirming her presence in Winterthur until at least ~06:00 CEST or in Flims on 11.10.?
translations.t0116: Bernasconi's vehicle (SG 77 310) exited the garage according to the garage log on 10.10. at 16:35 (local time, but note clock discrepancy). Is there a re-entry on 11.10. or further entries that rule out the vehicle returning during the night of the offence?
